actions.basis: I side with grok/minimax. The issue's own words set the bar: 'Whatever the remedy, a page whose dominant text direction is not horizontal must not ship as trusted native text in its current form. That part is not a design question' — and remedy (2) is explicitly conditional: 'Worth measuring first... That number decides whether (2) is warranted.' An ALREADY-FIXED claim must satisfy the issue's acceptance criteria, not every conditional alternative the issue floats. All three proofs survive: (1) fixed_by_commit 13033a3f7affffd9b642f29e80ae2a63e7a4ce28 is an ancestor of main_sha (git merge-base --is-ancestor, re-run by me); (2) acceptance mapped — binding requirement met at born_digital.py:1119 (refusal before extract_structured, prose retained, needs_ocr_enhancement + native_table_lane_refused set, landscape_page_refused event at orchestrator.py:767), detection uses the pre-existing dominant_text_direction as the issue required, remedy 1 implemented exactly as specified; (3) regression tests re-run BY ME at main_sha with the isolation canary passed: tests/test_landscape_detection_gh147.py + tests/test_landscape_refusal_a2_gh147.py, 20 passed. claude's reading demands remedy 2, which the issue itself declines to demand — that is the category error this batch was warned about (answering a question the issue did not ask). Closing also correctly kills pre-authored TICKET-E4, which would otherwise re-implement an existing fix — the exact PR-#250 failure shape.
